description: ElMazra3a Elsa3ida is competing in the NASA Space Apps Challenge: Field Shift. We are building a farmer-centered decision support tool that translates NASA satellite data like SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM, GRACE, and Landsat into actionable crop rotation strategies for soil health and climate resilience. We have passionate teammates in data science and spatial modeling, web development, agronomy, and UI/UX design or storytelling. Join ElMazra3a Elsa3ida to help adapt farms with NASA data!
summary:
welcome to ElMazra3a El Sa3ida  . it's an interactive agricultural decision-support tool and simulation platform tailored for smallholder farmers in Egypt & America  . It integrates an interactive field grid with satellite-derived Earth observations to track local soil health, root depth, and nutrient levels across farm plots.

How It Addresses the Challenge?   The platform directly addresses the challenge by combining  NASA climate datasets including long-term temperature trends and soil moisture observations with localized agricultural parameters and farmer priorities. Farmers can run real-time stress tests to simulate severe heatwaves and irrigation water reductions, allowing them to evaluate multi-season crop rotation strategies and project financial risks across historical weather patterns using probabilistic yield models.
Why It Is Important ? Faced with unpredictable climate fluctuations, water scarcity, and degrading soil quality, growers need data-driven rotation strategies to build farm resilience . By guiding strategic crop sequencing such as introducing nitrogen-fixing legumes after cereal crops the system restores soil fertility, reduces synthetic fertilizer reliance, conserves irrigation water, breaks recurring pest cycles, and safeguards farmer livelihoods even during adverse climate years
details:
ElMazra3a EL sa3ida — Crop Rotation Advisor is a bilingual (Arabic/English) web app that recommends a 3-season crop rotation for a specific field, based on NASA Earth observation data and a climate risk simulation.

1. Choose your land and previous crop

  • The farmer picks Egypt or the USA.
    • Egypt presets: Nile Delta – Gharbia, Minya, New Valley (priced in EGP/feddan).
    • USA presets: California Central Valley, Iowa Corn Belt, Kansas Wheat Belt (priced in USD/acre).
    • Any point on the map can also be clicked to update the coordinates.
  • The previous crop (Wheat, Potato, Tomato or Maize) sets the plant family. For example, wheat is Poaceae, and the app uses that to catch rotation clashes.
  • A toggle overlays the NASA MODIS NDVI vegetation-health layer on the satellite map.
  • The header shows live NASA indicators: the 10-year temperature anomaly (+0.74°C), SMAP soil moisture (46%) and the projected savings (11.1 urea sacks and 22% water).

2. Climate stress testing

  • One-click presets (Mild Season, Moderate Heat, Extreme Drought) and two sliders: extra heat wave (+0 to +4.5°C) and irrigation water deficit (0 to -45%).
  • Four data tabs: Soil Moisture (SMAP root-zone), Crop Health, 10-Yr Climate and SAR Radar. The soil moisture tab shows the root-zone value and a plain-language irrigation tip.

3. Compare three pathways

  • Smart Balanced Rotation (recommended): Soybean → Sugar Beet → Alfalfa/Berseem. Legumes fix nitrogen and cut urea use.
  • Cash-First Intensive (high risk): Maize → Potato → Wheat. It needs about 7.2 extra urea sacks and shows a botanical clash warning (-18%) because maize after wheat repeats the Poaceae family.
  • Climate & Water Resilient: Fava Bean → Sunflower → Sugar Beet. Deep-rooted, heat-tolerant crops that save 37% water.
  • Each card shows expected median income, worst-year income, urea sacks saved or needed and water saved.

4. Risk and tradeoff analysis for the selected pathway

  • A radar chart compares it against the cash baseline on five axes (the recommended rotation scores Cash Return 90, Water Saving 64, Soil Fertility 92, Heat Tolerance 61, Pest Break 87).
  • 10-year profit and risk bands show worst year (P10), median (P50) and best year (P90), with the cash baseline marked.
  • A 10-year historical replay (2015–2024) marks heatwave years in amber.
  • A "Why does this rotation protect your income and soil?" panel summarizes the logic.

5. AI Agronomy Copilot and field grid

  • The Gemini-powered copilot gives a plain-language recommendation based on the field's NDVI and root moisture.
  • The interactive field grid models 1 feddan (or acre) as 9 plots across three seasons. Each plot shows its crop, family and soil health (74–82%), plus season nitrogen (+50 kg), water use (1,900 m³) and root depth (115 cm).

6. Regional Data Blog

  • For six Egyptian governorates (Gharbia, Dakahlia, Beheira, Minya, Fayoum, New Valley) and the three US belts.
  • It includes region cards, monthly NASA POWER temperature charts, monthly GWETROOT root-wetness charts, an interactive correlation explorer and a 7×7 Pearson correlation matrix.
  • A crop suitability heatmap (11 crops × regions, scored 0–100) responds to the heat and water-weight sliders.
  • Key EDA findings and a "data quality caveats and how our engine solved them" section.

7. Farm Rescue (game)

  • A pixel-art teaching game built in Godot 4 and embedded in the site. It has a start screen, "How to play", saved best scores and a reset option.
  • Three scenarios on the same nine plots:

  • Players sow Wheat, Corn, Barley or Sunflower, each with its own water cost, growth time and maximum yield. They use the Water, Harvest and Plough-in tools while weather changes weekly (clear skies, overcast, heatwave, rain).
  • Each plot tracks moisture, salinity, nutrients and growth. Rotating to a different plant family restores nutrients, and heavy irrigation adds salt from the well.
  • The final score is out of 1,000: Crop Yield 30%, Water Efficiency 25%, Soil Health 25% and Sustainability 20%. A "Season in review" panel explains what went right or wrong.

Benefits

  • Lower costs: less urea (11.1 sacks saved in the Gharbia example) and 22% less irrigation water.
  • Income protection: the worst-year view compares downside risk across pathways, not only averages.
  • Soil health: legume rotation restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
  • Accessibility: Arabic/English, light/dark mode, local currency and area units, and a game for beginners.
  • Transparency: a "Raw NASA JSON" view and a "Judge Pitch" mode.

Intended impact

  • Give farmers satellite-based guidance on rotation choices, so decisions are based on measured soil moisture and heat trends.
  • Make farms more resilient to heat and drought and lower the water and fertilizer footprint of farming.
  • Use Farm Rescue to teach the same concepts to young people and beginner farmers.
  • Support regional planning: the heatmap shows which crops suit which governorate, for example New Valley's much lower suitability for maize and soybean.

Tools and technologies

  • NASA data: SMAP (soil moisture), MODIS Terra NDVI via GIBS, NASA POWER (2015–2024), MERRA-2 GWETROOT and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter.
  • Mapping: Leaflet with Esri World Imagery.
  • AI: Google Gemini for the Agronomy Copilot.
  • Game engine: Godot 4, served from the site's assets.
  • [Your stack]: front-end framework, languages, charting library, backend and hosting, and any AI-assisted tools you used.
  • Hardware: none beyond a browser, so it works on ordinary phones and laptops.

How it's creative

  • It turns NASA data into a decision and a money figure, not a dashboard.
  • It shows risk as P10/P50/P90 bands from a 10-year replay, so farmers see the worst case.
  • The stress sliders let users test their own farm against heat and drought before the season.
  • It flags botanical-family clashes automatically.
  • The AI copilot explains each recommendation in plain language.
  • Farm Rescue turns rotation, salinity and water budgeting into three playable challenges.
  • One engine works in two very different regions (Egypt and the US).

Factors the team considered

  • Coarse data: MERRA-2 cells are 0.5° × 0.625°, so Gharbia and Dakahlia share one cell. The engine separates them with local soil type and 250 m MODIS NDVI.
  • Climate risk needs more than one year: it uses the full 2015–2024 series to build the bands.
  • Irrigation isn't captured by the model: GWETROOT doesn't see canal pumping and NDVI is a single-date snapshot, so the app adds water-deficit sliders and SAR backscatter.
  • Regional differences: New Valley has the highest aridity stress (21% root moisture, NDVI 0.37), and Fayoum loses root moisture in summer, so recommendations vary by region.
  • Audience: language, units, currency and a beginner-friendly game. The game is labeled as simplified teaching data for a school activity.
